subject: Go-live: access cutover & rollback plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globex.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Onboarding <it-onboard@globex.com>, Marco Santoro <marco.santoro@globex.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Final cutover window and access dependencies

Hi Sofia,

We're lining up the go-live for Redwood on Friday, 2027-04-09 02:00-04:00 UTC and want to confirm the access cutover plan. Key asks from our side: SSO/SAML assertion timing, SCIM group mapping for 3 user groups (Payroll/Finance/Contractors), IP allowlist ranges for our shared office subnets, and a documented rollback plan if users cannot authenticate.

Can your team confirm the sequence and whether any short maintenance window is required on the Globex side? We have limited change freeze windows, so clarity will help our change board decision.

Also attaching our SCIM export so you can validate attribute mappings.

—Elena
Elena Rossi
Program Manager, IT Operations
Globex Finance

Attachments:
- globex-scim-export-20270402.csv (csv)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, IT Onboarding <it-onboard@globex.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Final cutover window and access dependencies

Thanks Elena — this is a great summary. High level plan below; I'll include the checklist and rollback playbook as attachments for the change board.

Planned sequence (Friday 2027-04-09, 02:00-04:00 UTC):
1) Pre-cutover verification (02:00-02:15) — verify SAML metadata exchange and cert fingerprints, confirm SCIM service account health.
2) SSO switch (02:15-02:35) — toggle AuthN routing to Redwood SAML IdP; monitor 1% canary users via group sampling.
3) SCIM sync (02:35-02:55) — run SCIM full sync for Payroll and Finance groups; validate group membership counts and attributes.
4) IP allowlist enforcement (02:55-03:10) — apply office subnet ranges in ACL to reduce noise, not required for initial auth but recommended before full rollout.
5) Production validation (03:10-03:40) — run login smoke tests, 10 business users exercise common flows, check logs for failed assertions.
6) Full cutover confirmation (03:40-04:00) — flip remaining routing and notify SRE/CS.

Rollback triggers and actions: any SSO assertion failure >5% of attempts across canary cohort, or SCIM sync causing group membership divergence >2% compared to baseline. Rollback actions in that case: revert AuthN routing to previous IdP snapshot (takes ~5 minutes) and run the rollback checklist (attached).

Notes/operational details:
- SCIM will use the service account named redwood-globex-scim. Karthik will share the key rotation window and TTL.
- We'll publish an IP allowlist CIDR set (office-eu-1) — this is optional pre-cutover; if Globex cannot change ACLs in time we will still proceed but monitor closely.
- We'll keep an open PagerDuty channel and Rancher logs accessible to your SRE for the window.

Attachments: redwood-sso-cutover-checklist.xlsx, rollback-playbook.pdf

Next steps: Karthik — can you confirm SCIM mapping and expected time for full sync? Marissa — can you confirm CS comms and the canary user list?

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globex.com>

Date: 2027-04-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Final cutover window and access dependencies

On Mon, Apr 3, 2027 at 11:05 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Notes/operational details:
> - SCIM will use the service account named redwood-globex-scim. Karthik will share the key rotation window and TTL.

Confirming SCIM details:
- Attribute mapping: mail -> userName, externalId -> id, groups -> groupMembership. I'll push a mapping file to the Drive link and attach a CSV that mirrors your export with our canonical attribute names.
- Expected full sync time: ~4 minutes for ~3k users over our staging pipeline; production sync should be 6–8 minutes given group expansions. We support incremental syncs post-cutover.
- Service account permissions: scim:read, scim:write, groups:read. Key TTL: 30 days for initial key; recommend rotating after go-live maintenance window.

IP allowlist: please confirm the public egress ranges for the office subnets; we'll add as office-eu-1 in our ACL. If you need a firewall rule change, provide the change ticket number and we'll coordinate the time slot.

I'll attach globex-scim-mapping.csv with the mapping and sample API curl for a test create/update.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:

Date: 2027-04-05T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Final cutover window and access dependencies

Thanks — this all looks good. Change board approved the Friday 02:00-04:00 UTC window contingent on us receiving the rollback-playbook.pdf and confirmation of the service account TTL.

Action items for Globex:
- Provide office egress CIDRs by EOD tomorrow (we'll create a firewall change ticket if needed).
- Provide canary user emails (we'll share a list of 12 users for the 1% sample).

We have one operational question: if we detect an assertion failure spike after SSO switch, is the revert fully automatic or does it require manual steps from Redwood? We prefer an automated flag to revert routing if the threshold is met.

Sofia — can you confirm whether the revert is a one-click toggle or manual and how long it will take? Also please send the final attachments to the change board.

Regards,
Elena
